title: Thai iced tea
summary: Very strong spiced black tea, sweetened while hot, poured over ice and crowned with a float of cream.

ingredients.note: brewed double strength (4 tea bags or 4 tsp loose tea per 2 cups water, steeped 5 minutes)
plus ice to fill the glasses

steps: Brew the tea with the cardamom and cinnamon in the hot water, steeping 5 minutes so it is darker than you would drink it plain.
Strain, then stir in the vanilla and allulose until dissolved. Let cool, then chill at least 30 minutes; hot tea melts the ice and dilutes the drink.
Fill two tall glasses with ice and pour in the tea, leaving room at the top.
Spoon 2 tbsp of cream over each glass so it floats and swirls down, and stir just before drinking.

swaps.note: or full-fat coconut milk for a lighter float

dairy_free_notes: Coconut cream floats and swirls the same way and adds a faint coconut flavour that suits the spices.
tips: Commercial Thai tea mixes are usually spiced (often with star anise) and coloured orange; this version approximates the spice with cardamom and cinnamon and will look brown, not orange.
Allulose dissolves fully in cold drinks, where erythritol can leave grit.

origin.history: Cha yen, iced milk tea, is sold by street vendors and cafés across Thailand. It is made from a strong black tea, typically a spiced, coloured blend, sweetened with sugar or condensed milk and finished with evaporated milk over ice. When and how the drink took its present form is not well documented.
